proposals.before: Through his mastery of documents and the law (wen Wuhai), he became the chief clerk of Pei.
proposals.after: Through his mastery of documents and faultless administration, he became the chief clerk of Pei.
proposals.reason: 文無害 is an administrative virtue phrase, not a personal name "Wuhai"; the parenthetical invents a false name.

proposals.before: The emperor laughed and said, 'So the Prime Minister has been looking after the people's interests!'
proposals.after: The emperor laughed and said, 'So the Prime Minister has been profiting from the people!'
proposals.reason: 利民 here is sarcastic (taking advantage of the people), not sincere "looking after their interests."

proposals.before: Everyone offered congratulations, but Zhao Ping alone came to offer condolences.
proposals.after: Everyone offered congratulations, but Shao Ping alone came to offer condolences.
proposals.reason: 召 as a surname is Shào; Zhao (趙) is a different surname.

proposals.before: Zhao Ping had been the Marquis of Dongling under the Qin dynasty.
proposals.after: Shao Ping had been the Marquis of Dongling under the Qin dynasty.
proposals.reason: 召平 should be Shao Ping, not Zhao Ping.

proposals.before: After Qin fell, he became a poor commoner and grew melons east of Chang'an. The melons were so fine that people called them 'Dongling melons' after his former title.
proposals.after: After Qin fell, he became a poor commoner and grew melons east of Chang'an. The melons were so fine that people called them 'Dongling melons' after Shao Ping's former title.
proposals.reason: Keep referent clear; surname 召 is Shao throughout this episode.

proposals.before: Zhao Ping said to the Prime Minister, 'This is where your troubles begin.
proposals.after: Shao Ping said to the Prime Minister, 'This is where your troubles begin.
proposals.reason: 召平 should be Shao Ping, not Zhao Ping.

decisions.reason: 文無害 is a clerkly virtue meaning faultless handling of documents, not a personal name; the literal's parenthetical "wen Wuhai" invents a false person, and "faultless administration" restores the sense.

After petitions accusing Xiao He of forcibly buying people's land cheaply, 上笑曰「夫相國乃利民」 is ironic; 利民 means taking profit from the people, not sincerely looking after their interests, and the handoff of the memorials for apology confirms the sarcasm.
The surname is 召 (Shào), not 趙 (Zhào); "Zhao Ping" misreads 召平, and "Shao Ping" corrects the English name while preserving the rest of the sentence.
召平者 names the same man as Shao Ping; rendering him Zhao Ping confuses 召 with 趙, and the replacement keeps the Dongling marquisate intact.

This unit already uses pronouns after 召平 has been identified; "after his former title" accurately glosses 東陵瓜／從召平以為名也 without inventing Zhao, so swapping in "Shao Ping's" is stylistic clarity rather than fixing an error in this sentence.
召平謂相國曰 again has the surname 召; "Zhao Ping" is the wrong romanization, and "Shao Ping" restores the speaker's name without changing the quoted warning.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0003 shows English Zhao Ping came only from misreading 召 as 趙; the personal-name claim must read Shao Ping while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
